answer.evidence: The tile is a flat plan view of stairs descending away from the viewer. Two stone panels fill the full 48px width: rows 1-15 (darker) and rows 16-31 (lighter). Each starts with a light 1-2 row edge line (rows 1-2 and row 16) and ends in a dark 1-row shadow (rows 14-15 and row 30). There is no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. The only vertical-looking parts are the 2-3px brown dirt strips at the left and right edges, which are the cut banks, not a receding side face. As terrain, the whole tile is a horizontal surface seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are at paving level (7 visible tones per tile against 7, 0% near-flat coverage), so there are no big flat fills. By eye, though, the stairs read as a few broad grey tread and riser bands with light edge lines and little per-stone shading. The paving reference shades each cobble individually with grain, and the grass reference has clumped tufts. The candidate has about 4 distinct lightness steps against the references' 5-6. Its dark edges are partly neutral (40% near-neutral) and partly tinted, which gives a mixed, slightly sticker-like outline. The piece is clean and readable but looks flatter and less textured than the references next to them, and the grass cliff side has little of the reference grass tuft variety. Doubt resolves to fail.
